name: Yuri Milner

summary.text: Yuri Milner is an investor whose firm Digital Sky Technologies (DST, later DST Global) invested $200 million in Facebook in May 2009 for a 1.96% stake at a $10 billion valuation, and then bought up to $100 million of stock from Facebook employees. With his wife Julia he co-founded the Breakthrough Prizes in 2012 together with Sergey Brin, Priscilla Chan and Mark Zuckerberg, and Anne Wojcicki; the prizes award $3 million each in life sciences, fundamental physics and mathematics. In 2015 he launched the Breakthrough Initiatives with Stephen Hawking, including the $100 million Breakthrough Listen program. In November 2017 the ICIJ's Paradise Papers reporting linked Russian state-owned VTB Bank and a Gazprom subsidiary to funding behind DST's Twitter and Facebook investments; Milner said less than 5% of his firm's funding came from Russian government institutions.

facts.claim: On May 26, 2009 Facebook announced that Digital Sky Technologies (DST), Milner's investment firm, would invest $200 million in preferred stock for a 1.96% stake at a $10 billion valuation, without taking a board seat. In July 2009 DST agreed to buy up to $100 million of common stock from Facebook employees and former employees.

facts.claim: Milner and his wife Julia co-founded the Breakthrough Prizes in 2012 with Sergey Brin, Priscilla Chan and Mark Zuckerberg, and Anne Wojcicki. The prizes, funded by the founders' personal foundations, award $3 million each annually in life sciences, fundamental physics and mathematics.

facts.claim: ICIJ reported on November 5, 2017, from the Paradise Papers, that Russian state-controlled VTB Bank put $191 million into a Milner fund that was invested in Twitter, and that a subsidiary of state-controlled Gazprom funded an offshore company, Kanton Services, that took part in the Facebook deal and held about $1 billion of Facebook shares shortly before the 2012 IPO. Milner said his investments were made on business merits, that he had been unaware of the Gazprom link, and that less than 5% of his firm's funding came from Russian government institutions. Facebook said the Gazprom-linked vehicle was a passive investor with no voting rights or board seat.
facts.quote: VTB put $191 million into Milner's fund, which was invested in Twitter.

openQuestions: The site pairs Milner with Jeff Bezos as longevity funders (Altos Labs); no source for either's Altos Labs investment was retrieved, so no connection to jeff-bezos was recorded.
Earlier Breakthrough Prize pages name Jack Ma and Cathy Zhang among the founders; later pages omit them.
The year of the VTB-funded Twitter investment is given as 2011 by some outlets and 2013 by Quartz.
